thought.text: Catalog parsed and 45 valid records emitted. The catalog references port 8000; let me serve there for a fully successful run.

reasoning_content: The end-to-end run produced 45 records. URLs point to port 8000 in the catalog, not 8123 — so the actual resource fetches failed by connection refused, but the catalog parsing and processing worked (downloaded catalog, parsed, emitted valid JSONL records, exit 0). Let me serve on 8000 to get a fully successful run for stronger evidence. Let me kill 8123 and start 8000.

action.command:
cd /workspace && ps aux | grep "[h]ttp.server 8123" | awk '{print $2}' | xargs -r kill; (cd tests/data && python3 -m http.server 8000 >/tmp/httpd8000.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1.5 && curl -s -o /dev/null -w "server HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8000/catalog.ttl && poetry run python dcat_catalog_check.py --url http://localhost:8000/catalog.ttl > /tmp/e2e2.jsonl 2>/tmp/e2e2.err; echo "e2e exit=$?"; echo "lines=$(wc -l < /tmp/e2e2.jsonl)"; echo "good_checks_true=$(grep -c '"accessible": true' /tmp/e2e2.jsonl)"; python3 -c "
import json
recs=[json.loads(l) for l in open('/tmp/e2e2.jsonl')]
good=[r for r in recs if r.get('accessible')]
bad=[r for r in recs if not r.get('accessible')]
print('total',len(recs),'accessible',len(good),'inaccessible',len(bad))
print('sample good:',json.dumps(good[0]) if good else None)
";
